summary.text: Khaleel Anderson is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party Assembly member for District 31 in southeast Queens, elected in November 2020. A community organizer from the Rockaways, he began organizing as a teenager and served on Queens Community Board 14 before entering the Assembly at age 24. He is running unopposed in the November 3, 2026 general election.

paragraphs.text: Born in Brooklyn and raised in the Rockaways; lives in Far Rockaway, Queens.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Queens College (2019, per Ballotpedia); the Assembly biography says he was finalizing a master's degree in Urban Affairs there, with a minor in Cities and Social Medicine.
Began as a community organizer at age 13; in 2011 he was an organizer for a local nonprofit that trains cohorts of youth in civic engagement.

Before his election he worked as a student and community activist and helped build a half-acre urban farm that provides fresh produce, healthy-eating workshops and trainings, and jobs for young people.
Was the youngest member of Queens Community Board 14 and of his local Police Precinct Council during his tenure.

Won the open Assembly District 31 seat in the November 2020 general election at age 24 against Republican Joseph Cullina, according to his campaign website's reprint of a news report; his campaign site and the Assembly describe him as the youngest Black Assembly member in New York State history.
Named a 2021 Lindsay Fellow in Government Leadership and Practice, according to his Assembly biography.

Chairs the Assembly Task Force on Food, Farm & Nutrition Policy and serves on the Children and Families, Energy, Environmental Conservation, Insurance, Labor, and People with Disabilities committees in the 2025-2026 session.

According to his Assembly biography, his priorities include housing and healthcare justice, criminal justice reform, educational equity, transportation equity and environmental justice; he also cites food insecurity and disaster preparedness.
